title: GPU provisioner abstraction: Terraform module for mixed ASG + Karpenter autoscaling in private VPC
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers require a robust Terraform module that can provision GPU-backed compute for inference workloads while supporting both ASG-backed nodegroups and Karpenter-managed spot/ondemand mixes. Existing modules are fragmented across repos and do not include safe driver/OS upgrade automation, healthcheck probes, or a clear canary/rollback strategy for kernel/driver changes.

Goal: Deliver a single terraform module (terraform/modules/gpu-provisioner) that: 1) declares heterogeneous GPU pools (ASG for reserved capacity + Karpenter provisioners for burst capacity), 2) wires up node lifecycle hooks and healthchecks used by our private control plane, 3) integrates OS/driver upgrade orchestration with safe canary drains and automatic rollback, 4) exposes config toggles for batching-friendly labels/taints and node pool QoS settings.

Scope (what this ticket covers): module API design, Terraform implementation, example private VPC composition, CI tests (plan/apply in a sandbox), documented upgrade playbook, and handoff notes for on-call & solutions engineering. Does NOT include production rollout to customer-owned VPCs (separate rollout ticket).

Implementation notes / decisions: - Module will create two primary resource families: aws_autoscaling_group (reserved gpu_asg) and a set of Karpenter provisioner manifests (rendered via helm provider or local_file manifest). - Use user-data + SSM parameter bootstrap to install NVIDIA drivers via our vetted AMI bootstrap script (AMI id remains a variable for customers who bring their own). - Provide optional Lifecycle hooks (ASG lifecycle hook + Lambda/SSM handler) to perform pre-terminate checks and drain logic. - Healthcheck: add a cloudwatch/alb target + k8s node-problem-detector integration to mark nodes unhealthy; Terraform will provision alarm and a lambda that can move capacity or notify on-call. - Upgrade strategy: provide blue/green nodegroup upgrade via capacity replacement for ASG and a staged taint/drain for Karpenter provisioners with automated verification using a user-provided smoke-test URL or probe. - Backwards compatibility: module inputs will support legacy variable names via deprecated variables with warnings. - Security: IAM least-privilege for the module, KMS key id injection, and audit log hooks enabled by default.

Acceptance criteria (high-level): - Terraform module accepted by infra review and merged to main. - Module can reproducibly create ASG+Karpenter compute in our staging VPC and pass the end-to-end smoke test. - Upgrade path executed in sandbox demonstrating canary replacement and automated rollback on smoke-test failure. - Documentation and runbook published (Confluence) and infra-team walkthrough completed.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes a stable interface (variables/outputs) and example composition for private VPC use
Provisioning run in sandbox creates ASG (reserved) + Karpenter provisioner (burst) with GPU AMIs and node labels required by runtime
Automated smoke test that validates model-serving pods warm and inference endpoint returns 200 within defined latency thresholds
Upgrade playbook executed: trigger driver/AMI upgrade, observe canary node, verify smoke test, and automatically rollback on failure
Healthcheck alarms create tickets via PagerDuty stub and do not trigger false positives during normal scaling
Code reviewed and merged; integration tests pass in CI pipeline
